Distinct-value count (4686) is also far higher than the more curated-looking 'basecolor' (1613), implying 'color' is the noisier, less-normalized of the two color fields.

Sample values ('acacia','acrylic','aged brass') are actually material/finish names rather than basic hues -- common in furniture/hardware where 'color' is conventionally named after the material or plating (brass, walnut, espresso). 112 distinct values ranging from a bare number ('1') to short phrases ('1 year') to full sentences ('1 year from the date of purchase.'), so despite the name implying a simple duration, the raw data is not cleanly structured; numeric_parseable_fraction is only 0.0003 even though many values start with a digit, meaning the number is usually attached to text rather than standalone. uniqueness_ratio 0.9785 (near one-to-one with occurrences) is a classic identifier signature, but the name ('sample' + 'part number') strongly suggests an internal reference -- either the part number of the physical sample unit used for photography/QA, or possibly a separately-orderable fabric/material swatch -- rather than a value any shopper would know or type.
